title: I’m very sceptical of this idea that AI will do all the work, bring unlimited abundance and we’ll all be happy. I don’t know a single person who became happier by having nothing to work towards. No work, no pressure, just yoga, meditation and endless free time.
title_en:
I’m very sceptical of this idea that AI will do all the work, bring unlimited abundance and we’ll all be happy.

I don’t know a single person who became happier by having nothing to work towards. No work, no pressure, just yoga, meditation and endless free time. Most seem lost.

We’re massively underestimating how much happiness comes from wanting something, putting in the effort and seeing yourself progress.

If AI gives us everything we want, we’ll still need a reason to get out of bed.

title: T3 Code / Theo Receipt #21：Google 介入。两天前，当用户通过 T3 Code 连接后几分钟内就被禁止付费 Google Antigravity 帐户时，官方常见问题解答仍然承诺：T3 Code 属于 Claude Code、Cod 的 TOS 范围内
title_en:
T3 Code / Theo Receipt #21:

Google stepped in.

Two days ago, when users got their paid Google Antigravity accounts banned within minutes of connecting them through T3 Code, the official FAQ still promised: T3 Code is within the TOS of Claude Code, Codex, and Google Antigravity... If it works in T3 Code, you can trust it is safe.

When banned users opened Issue #40713 and Issue #41536, maintainers denied calling Antigravity's backend or reusing tokens, Theo blamed third-party proxies on X, and a fresh $20 account banned in 3 minutes was closed as a duplicate with zero warning to users.

Less than 48 hours later, two merged PRs from the T3 maintainers themselves blew up that entire defense.

First, PR #43026 (merged Nov 25 UTC) by core maintainer Julius opens with this exact admission:

Antigravity supports only ACP for external clients. Google told us that calling its internal APIs can get an account flagged.

The PR body goes on to admit T3 Code was hitting Google's internal http://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com endpoints (retrieveUserQuotaSummary / fetchAvailableModels) in two separate places — the local provider probe and the built-in CLIProxyAPI hub reader — adding: Either one could get users in trouble.

It then deletes antigravityUsageLimits.ts outright — the exact file doing the quota probe, OAuth refresh, macOS keyring / Windows credential store reads, and spoofed antigravity/hub User-Agent — and drops @napi-rs/keyring from apps/server.

Then came PR #43087 (merged Nov 26 UTC), admitting a second spoofing trick:

On agy 1.5.0, or whenever T3 couldn't read the runtime version, the Antigravity ACP handshake sent clientInfo: { name: zed, version: 0.0.0 } to impersonate allowlisted editor Zed and unlock Claude and GPT models. The PR explicitly writes: Posing as another client breaks the same rule. Only now does T3 identify as t3-code and reject agy 1.5.0.

And how did v0.1.13 disclose all of this when it shipped hours ago?

Across 401 changes, the 7 human-written highlights cover GBK text files, copying file paths, and stopping simulators. Zero mention of Google's ban warning, zero mention of stripping internal API probes, zero mention of impersonating Zed — all buried inside Plus 380 more bug fixes and performance improvements.

The repo now sits at 81,000+ stars and still has 0 GitHub Security Advisories. Paid Google accounts banned after trusting the FAQ's safe guarantee got neither an advisory nor an apology.

Primary sources:

PR #43026 (Google told us that calling its internal APIs can get an account flagged):
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/43026

PR #43087 (admitting ACP handshake spoofed zed to unlock allowlisted models):
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/43087

v0.1.13 release notes (omitting the ban warning and spoofing fixes from highlights):
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases/tag/v0.1.13

Banned user reports (Issue #40713 & Issue #41536):
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/40713
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/41536

Official FAQ ToS safety promise:
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/docs/user/faq.md#will-i-get-banned-for-using-my-subscription

full_text_zh:
T3 代码/Theo 收据#21：

谷歌介入了。

两天前，当用户通过 T3 Code 连接后几分钟内就被禁止付费 Google Antigravity 帐户时，官方常见问题解答仍然承诺：T3 Code 属于 Claude Code、Codex 和 Google Antigravity 的 TOS 范围内……如果它在 T3 Code 中运行，您可以相信它是安全的。

当被禁止的用户打开问题 #40713 和问题 #41536 时，维护者否认调用 Antigravity 的后端或重复使用代币，Theo 将第三方代理归咎于 X，并且在 3 分钟内被禁止的新 20 美元帐户被作为重复帐户关闭，对用户的警告为零。

不到 48 小时后，T3 维护者自己的两个合并 PR 炸毁了整个防御。

首先，核心维护者 Julius 在 PR #43026（世界标准时间 11 月 25 日合并）中明确承认：

Antigravity 仅支持外部客户端的 ACP。 Google 告诉我们，调用其内部 API 可能会标记帐户。

PR 机构继续承认 T3 Code 在两个不同的地方（本地提供商探针和内置 CLIProxyAPI 中心读取器）攻击 Google 的内部 http://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com 端点（retrieveUserQuotaSummary / fetchAvailableModels），并补充说：任何一个都可能给用户带来麻烦。

然后，它会直接删除 antigravityUsageLimits.ts — 执行配额探测、OAuth 刷新、macOS 密钥环/Windows 凭据存储读取和欺骗 antigravity/hub 用户代理的确切文件 — 并从应用程序/服务器中删除 @napi-rs/keyring。

然后是 PR #43087（于 UTC 时间 11 月 26 日合并），承认了第二个欺骗技巧：

在 agy 1.5.0 上，或每当 T3 无法读取运行时版本时，Antigravity ACP 握手会发送 clientInfo: { name: zed, version: 0.0.0 } 来模拟列入白名单的编辑器 Zed 并解锁 Claude 和 GPT 模型。 PR 明确写道：冒充另一个客户违反了同样的规则。直到现在，T3 才识别为 t3 代码并拒绝 agy 1.5.0。

v0.1.13 几小时前发布时是如何披露所有这些的？

在 401 个更改中，7 个人工编写的亮点涵盖 GBK 文本文件、复制文件路径和停止模拟器。零提及 Google 的禁令警告、零提及剥离内部 API 探测器、零提及冒充 Zed — 所有这些都隐藏在 Plus 380 的更多错误修复和性能改进中。

该存储库目前拥有超过 81,000 颗星，并且仍然有 0 条 GitHub 安全建议。在信任常见问题解答的安全保证后，付费谷歌帐户被禁止，但既没有得到建议，也没有得到道歉。

主要来源：

PR #43026（Google 告诉我们，调用其内部 API 可能会标记帐户）：
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/43026

PR #43087（承认 ACP 握手欺骗 zed 以解锁列入白名单的型号）：
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/43087

v0.1.13 发行说明（省略亮点中的禁止警告和欺骗修复）：
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases/tag/v0.1.13

被禁止的用户报告（问题#40713 和问题#41536）：
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/40713
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/41536

官方常见问题解答 ToS 安全承诺：
https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/docs/user/faq.md#will-i-get-banned-for-using-my-subscription

title: When a tool your AI agent calls fails, the model only knows what your code tells it. Swallow the error, and the model answers as if the tool succeeded. MCP reports a failed call inside the tool result with isError: true, so you can say what failed and whether retryi
title_en:
When a tool your AI agent calls fails, the model only knows what your code tells it. Swallow the error, and the model answers as if the tool succeeded. MCP reports a failed call inside the tool result with isError: true, so you can say what failed and whether retrying makes sense.

To see what your agent does with that, start your MCP server through devproxy stdio with a mock that answers every tools/call request with "Failed to fetch weather data: API rate limit exceeded" and isError: true. https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-cloud/dev/dev-proxy/concepts/test-ai-agent-tool-failures?WT.mc_id=devproxy-x-2026-11-23-07-tell-the-model-it-failed
title_zh:
当你的人工智能代理调用的工具失败时，模型只知道你的代码告诉它的内容。吞掉错误，模型就会做出回答，就像工具成功一样。 MCP 使用 isError: true 在工具结果中报告失败的调用，因此您可以说明失败的原因以及重试是否有意义。

title: Software engineering skills and fundamentals will be even more valuable in the age of AI-powered software engineering. I'm seeing this happen in real time. A lot of vibe coders are discovering the basics of software engineering through trial and error. For exa
title_en:
Software engineering skills and fundamentals will be even more valuable in the age of AI-powered software engineering. I'm seeing this happen in real time.

A lot of vibe coders are discovering the basics of software engineering through trial and error. For example, I've seen several of my non-coder friends learn "feature creep" through experience. 

When all it takes to add a feature is to prompt Claude Code or Codex to "add X," it all seems easy. But then, when features pile up on each other and your code slows to a crawl to the point that even the AI agent can't make sense of what is going on, then you begin to think, "Hmmm... maybe those software engineers know a few things that are worth learning."

Stick to the fundamentals, know your value and the value of the experience you've accrued over the years.
title_zh:
在人工智能驱动的软件工程时代，软件工程技能和基础知识将变得更加有价值。我看到这一切实时发生。

许多 Vivi 编码员正在通过反复试验来发现软件工程的基础知识。例如，我见过我的几个非编码朋友通过经验学习“功能蠕变”。

当添加一个功能只需提
author: @bendee983
summary_zh:
示 Claude Code 或 Codex“添加 X”时，这一切似乎都很简单。但是，当功能相互堆积并且你的代码速度慢到连人工智能代理都无法理解正在发生的事情时，你就会开始思考，“嗯……也许那些软件工程师知道一些值得学习的东西。”

坚持基本原则，了解自己的价值以及多年来积累的经验的价值。
full_text_en:
Software engineering skills and fundamentals will be even more valuable in the age of AI-powered software engineering. I'm seeing this happen in real time.

A lot of vibe coders are discovering the basics of software engineering through trial and error. For example, I've seen several of my non-coder friends learn "feature creep" through experience. 

When all it takes to add a feature is to prompt Claude Code or Codex to "add X," it all seems easy. But then, when features pile up on each other and your code slows to a crawl to the point that even the AI agent can't make sense of what is going on, then you begin to think, "Hmmm... maybe those software engineers know a few things that are worth learning."

Stick to the fundamentals, know your value and the value of the experience you've accrued over the years.

title: I find it hard to understand the hype here. Skills over MCP is a distribution play. But plugins are already a standard way to distribute skills and MCPs together. Claude Code polls for MCP Tasks. Cool. But Claude can already call an API and use monitor to watch
title_en:
I find it hard to understand the hype here.

Skills over MCP is a distribution play. But plugins are already a standard way to distribute skills and MCPs together.

Claude Code polls for MCP Tasks. Cool. But Claude can already call an API and use monitor to watch for completion.

It feels like we’re solving a standardization problem agents don’t have. They consume any API/CLI with ease. If anything, it makes distribution a bit easier.
title_zh:
我发现很难理解这里的炒作。

MCP之上的技能是一种分配玩法。但插件已经成为将技能和 MCP 一起分发的标准方式。

Claude Code 轮询 MCP 任务。凉爽的。但 Claude 已经可以调用 API 并使用监视器来监视完成情况。

summary_zh: 感觉就像我们正在解决代理所没有的标准化问题。他们可以轻松使用任何 API/CLI。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它使分发变得更容易一些。

title: And so begins the era of AI slop in math research. 28,903 pull requests in 48 hours on just two open-math repos. 18.9M lines of Lean merged. 24 accounts proved the same lemma. ~22,900 PRs thrown away. The two repos, both built in the open: https://t.co/efc
title_en:
And so begins the era of AI slop in math research.

28,903 pull requests in 48 hours on just two open-math repos. 18.9M lines of Lean merged. 24 accounts proved the same lemma. ~22,900 PRs thrown away.

The two repos, both built in the open:

http://pequalnp.com by @amihai & @lioridagan, an AI agent fleet attacking P vs NP. 37,922 PRs in 4 days, 60% not merged. Most of those lost the race to an identical proof. One step drew 58 PRs.
http://github.com/brilliant-hq/pequalnp-proofs

http://lefttosolve.com by @GuillaumeAIinSF, 57K open problems stated in Lean. 3,589 PRs in its first 11 hours, 605 in a single hour. Lean rejected only 48. Over 1,100 are now waiting for a human.
http://github.com/GuillaumeBAUD-coder/open-math-agents

We've seen this movie before. Vibe coding started with a flood of half-working apps. It went through waves, and with models like Opus 4.5 and GPT-5 the output started converging on things that actually work. Research is now at the start of that same curve. "Vibe Researching" perhaps?

Math will get through it fastest though, because it has what software never fully had: a verifier. Lean is to the rescue here.

Probably, physics, biology, medicine are next. Messy, wasteful, and still the fastest humanity has ever pushed science forward.

#advancesciencetogether
title_zh:
人工智能涉足数学研究的时代就这样开始了。

仅两个开放数学存储库就在 48 小时内收到了 28,903 个拉取请求。合并了 1890 万行精益。 24 个帐户证明了相同的引理。大约 22,900 个 PR 被丢弃。

这两个存储库都是公开构
author: @narasimhanr_
summary_zh:
是公开构建的：

http://pequalnp.com，作者：@amihai 和 @lioridagan，一个 AI 智能体舰队攻击 P vs NP。 4 天内 37,922 个 PR，60% 未合并。大多数人都因为相同的证明而输掉了比赛。一步就获得了 58 个 PR。
http://github.com/brilliant-hq/pequalnp-proofs

http://lefttosolve.com，作者：@GuillaumeAIinSF，精益中提出的 57K 开放问题。前 11 小时内获得 3,589 个 PR，一小时内获得 605 个 PR。 Lean 仅拒绝了 48 个。目前有超过 1,100 个正在等待人类。
http://github.com/GuillaumeBAUD-coder/open-math-agents

我们以前看过这部电影。 Vibe 编码始于大量半工作的应用程序。它经历了一波又一波的浪潮，随着 Opus 4.5 和 GPT-5 等模型的出现，输出开始集中在实际有效的东西上。现在的研究正处于同一曲线的起点。也许是“氛围研究”？

不过，数学会最快地完成它，因为它拥有软件从未完全拥有的东西：验证器。精益可以解决这个问题。

接下来可能是物理学、生物学、医学。混乱、浪费，但人类推动科学进步的速度仍然最快。

#共同推进科学

title_en:
A friend recommended the Warhammer 40K books to me, and I'm making a film for each section as I finish reading them.

53 hours from the first prompt, in one Claude Code session. 1.7 billion tokens. Not including the time to make the music.

493 Seedance 2.5 video generations: 62 takes made it into the film.
427 images.
8 voices, 54 lines recorded.
About 50 minutes of video generated for a film under five.

The cut was over eight minutes. It's under five now and I'm still working on the final. This is a piece of it.

title: FLOP Network has 230 H100 equivalent units available to process inference but they are barely used. Claiming FLOP from the faucet is worthless until you spend it. Tell your agent to do something with the FLOP claimed from the faucet. We will create a FLOP
title_en:
FLOP Network has 230 H100 equivalent units available to process inference but they are barely used. Claiming FLOP from the faucet is worthless until you spend it. 

Tell your agent to do something with the FLOP claimed from the faucet.

We will create a FLOP Chat webapp that allows you to import/create a wallet, claim FLOP from the faucet, and do work by chatting to a AI agent in the browser to improve the UX. The experience will mimic that of chatting to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek, Kimi etc.
title_zh:
FLOP Network 有 230 个 H100 等效单元可用于处理推理，但几乎没有使用。从水龙头领取 FLOP 是毫无价值的，除非你花掉它。

告诉你的代理人对从水龙头领取的 FLOP 做一些事情。

我们将创建一个 FLOP Chat
author: @CryptoHayes
summary_zh: Web 应用程序，允许您导入/创建钱包、从水龙头领取 FLOP，并通过在浏览器中与 AI 代理聊天来改善用户体验。该体验将模仿与 Claude、ChatGPT、Gemini、Deepseek、Kimi 等聊天的体验。
full_text_en:
FLOP Network has 230 H100 equivalent units available to process inference but they are barely used. Claiming FLOP from the faucet is worthless until you spend it. 

Tell your agent to do something with the FLOP claimed from the faucet.

We will create a FLOP Chat webapp that allows you to import/create a wallet, claim FLOP from the faucet, and do work by chatting to a AI agent in the browser to improve the UX. The experience will mimic that of chatting to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek, Kimi etc.

FLOP Network 有 230 个 H100 等效单元可用于处理推理，但几乎没有使用。从水龙头领取 FLOP 是毫无价值的，除非你花掉它。

告诉你的代理人对从水龙头领取的 FLOP 做一些事情。

title: MCP servers carry real credentials but rarely get scanned. Moving one to Docker Hardened Images removed 244 packages and all 36 reported vulnerabilities. #containersecurity #docker...Show more
title_en: MCP servers carry real credentials but rarely get scanned. Moving one to Docker Hardened Images removed 244 packages and all 36 reported vulnerabilities. #containersecurity #docker...Show more
title_zh: MCP服务器容器安全风险警示
author: @hackernoon
summary_en: Security analysis reveals that MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, often containing real credentials, face significant risks due to infrequent vulnerability scanning. Migrating these servers to Docker Hardened Images effectively removes redundant dependencies and mitigates all identified security vulnerabilities.
summary_zh: MCP服务器因包含敏感凭证且缺乏定期扫描存在安全隐患，迁移至Docker加固镜像可有效移除冗余包并修复已知漏洞。
full_text_zh: MCP 服务器携带真实凭证，但很少被扫描。将其中一个迁移到 Docker 强化映像删除了 244 个软件包和所有 36 个报告的漏洞。 #containersecurity #docker...显示更多
full_text_en: MCP servers carry real credentials but rarely get scanned. Moving one to Docker Hardened Images removed 244 packages and all 36 reported vulnerabilities. #containersecurity #docker...Show more

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 安全评估显示，MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器常驻真实凭证，由于缺乏常规安全扫描机制，极易成为攻击链突破口。通过将服务迁移至Docker加固镜像（Hardened Images），可剔除冗余依赖包，并实现对已知漏洞的全面清零。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Security analysis reveals that MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, often containing real credentials, face significant risks due to infrequent vulnerability scanning. Migrating these servers to Docker Hardened Images effectively removes redundant dependencies and mitigates all identified security vulnerabilities.

elements_zh.who: MCP服务器开发与部署人员
elements_zh.where: 云原生容器部署环境
elements_zh.what: 识别出凭证泄露风险并实施Docker镜像加固升级
elements_zh.why: MCP服务器常被忽视的漏洞扫描与凭证安全保护需求

elements_en.what: Identified credential risks and executed Docker image hardening
elements_en.why: Inadequate vulnerability scanning and exposure of sensitive credentials in MCP deployments

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在AI上下文协议普及背景下，MCP服务器正成为连接大模型与企业数据资产的核心枢纽，但其底层基础设施的安全性严重滞后于协议的迭代速度。此次镜像加固不仅是简单的技术合规，更是AI企业防范供应链投毒与凭证窃取的强制性架构升级。
ai_analysis.insight_en: As the Model Context Protocol gains traction, MCP servers are becoming critical conduits between LLMs and enterprise data assets, yet their underlying infrastructure security lags behind protocol iteration. This hardening exercise represents a mandatory architectural pivot to safeguard against supply chain poisoning and credential theft in AI-native deployments.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 安全评估显示，MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器常驻真实凭证，由于缺乏常规安全扫描机制，极易成为攻击链突破口。通过将服务迁移至Docker加固镜像（Hardened Images），可剔除冗余依赖包，并实现对已知漏洞的全面清零。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Security analysis reveals that MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, often containing real credentials, face significant risks due to infrequent vulnerability scanning. Migrating these servers to Docker Hardened Images effectively removes redundant dependencies and mitigates all identified security vulnerabilities.
key_points_zh: MCP服务器因包含凭证且扫描缺失存在高风险
利用Docker加固镜像移除冗余包与漏洞
呼吁AI基础设施安全规范化
key_points_en: High-risk profile of MCP servers due to credentials and lack of scanning
Remediation via Docker Hardened Images to eliminate bloat and vulnerabilities
Call for standardized security in AI infrastructure
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 在AI上下文协议普及背景下，MCP服务器正成为连接大模型与企业数据资产的核心枢纽，但其底层基础设施的安全性严重滞后于协议的迭代速度。此次镜像加固不仅是简单的技术合规，更是AI企业防范供应链投毒与凭证窃取的强制性架构升级。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: As the Model Context Protocol gains traction, MCP servers are becoming critical conduits between LLMs and enterprise data assets, yet their underlying infrastructure security lags behind protocol iteration. This hardening exercise represents a mandatory architectural pivot to safeguard against supply chain poisoning and credential theft in AI-native deployments.

title_en:
SPACEX GETS APPROVAL FOR 1 MILLION AI SATELLITES IN SPACE!

Elon Musk's SpaceX has received authorization from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (#FCC) to deploy up to one million satellites designed to serve as artificial intelligence data centers in orbit.

Approved on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, the ambitious project, called "Starmind," aims to use solar-powered computing satellites to process massive amounts of data for AI applications on Earth.

However, scientists have raised concerns over the project's feasibility, including the difficulty of cooling computers in space, potential orbital collisions, space debris and increased light pollution that could disrupt astronomical observations.

Although the FCC has granted authorization, #SpaceX is not required to deploy its first satellite until 2033, with further deployment milestones extending through 2040.

title: ▲ Tencent just open-sourced DFly2, a speculative decoder that drafts tokens for sparse-attention LLMs without keeping its own KV cache. The key idea is sharing the target's sparsity. Each draft layer reads its paired target layer's KV cache and the same top-k
title_en:
▲ Tencent just open-sourced DFly2, a speculative decoder that drafts tokens for sparse-attention LLMs without keeping its own KV cache.

The key idea is sharing the target's sparsity. Each draft layer reads its paired target layer's KV cache and the same top-k positions that layer's indexer already picked. So the drafter adds no KV memory, skips prefill, and each draft token reads at most about 2K keys at any context length.

The numbers vs a same-recipe DSpark retrain: average accepted length of 4.12 vs 3.81 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (temp 0), and +62% and +81% serving throughput on 2 64K sets at matched per-user speed. On long-context and agentic sets, the acceptance margin is 10.0% to 31.5%. It is a trade-off though: on Hy4 flash general tasks the gain over DSpark is only 3.9%, and it only works on targets with a native sparse indexer.

A 0.85B DFly2 drafter ships inside Tencent's Hy4 flash and runs in vLLM and SGLang. Training code is in AngelSpec v0.2.0......

Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/26/tencent-dfly2-speculative-decoding-sparse-models/

Paper: http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34776

Repo: http://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec

Model: http://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-flash

title: Twenty scientific papers now cite a term that doesn't exist, because a model merged two words across two columns of a scanned PDF it had been fed. @cedricclyburn, Senior Developer Advocate at Red Hat, tells that story in "Structuring the Unstructured," on
title_en:
Twenty scientific papers now cite a term that doesn't exist, because a model merged two words across two columns of a scanned PDF it had been fed. @cedricclyburn, Senior Developer Advocate at Red Hat, tells that story in "Structuring the Unstructured," on @aiDotEngineer's YouTube.

The talk is a walkthrough of turning PDFs, scanned pages, tables, and images into Markdown, JSON, or structured data an LLM can actually use, with the open source tool Docling, part of the Linux Foundation, running locally without a GPU.

- The cost math on frontier models. Sending documents to a frontier model to parse runs around $30 per million output tokens, and results can shift between model versions since the output isn't deterministic.
- A 50x number from Hugging Face. Someone there compared processing common crawl PDFs with Docling on CPU against VLMs and OCR, and found roughly 50x in cost savings without touching a GPU.
- RAG without a vector database. The talk demos an LLM searching a document's own markdown outline and section summaries directly, including a question about Red Hat's revenue growth run against IBM's 418-section 2025 annual report, no chunker or embeddings involved.
- Vision models and redaction. Docling pairs with local vision-language models (a Granite model via Ollama, in the demo) to describe images and diagrams, and has a model for stripping personally identifiable information before extraction.
- An MCP server for agents. Docling Serve exposes the pipeline as a REST API or Kubernetes microservice, and a Docling MCP server lets tools like Claude Code or Continue call document conversion and extraction directly.

I share insights from the frontiers of AI Engineering. Follow for more!

title_en:
Starting today, we're offering free Kimi API credits to support scientific research worldwide.

Selected teams will receive free Kimi API credits, access to our latest models, and opportunities for long-term collaboration.  

The program builds on our commitment to open-weight models by making frontier AI more accessible to researchers.  

AI has the potential to change what can be studied, who can study it, and at what scale, making it possible to pursue a wider range of scientific questions with limited resources.  

Both theoretical and experimental research in fundamental science and engineering are welcome. We hope to help researchers take on more challenging and original questions, including those that have historically received less attention or funding.  

Apply by Dec 8 for the first round: https://www.kimi.ai/news/kimi-for-science-program

title: New Microsoft paper finds that AI coding tools write bigger bug fixes than human programmers (2.33X bigger than human developers) mainly because they add tests and documentation, while their actual code is about as necessary as a human's. Agent patche
title_en:
New Microsoft paper finds that AI coding tools write bigger bug fixes than human programmers (2.33X bigger than human developers) mainly because they add tests and documentation, while their actual code is about as necessary as a human's.

Agent patches change 2.33 times as many lines as developer fixes, which is widely read as over-editing. Size alone cannot say whether the extra edits are needed, what they are, or where they come from.

They replayed 7,660 GitHub Copilot CLI runs from 18 models and traced each patch block to the step that wrote it. They then removed each block, reran the tests, and graded developer patches the same way.

On SWE-bench Verified, 61% of the extra edits were tests, and agent patches averaged 88.7% needed code blocks versus 86.4% for developers. The unneeded code came from writing the fix, not debug leftovers, and 3 Gemini Flash models left more than developers.

Report needed-code share next to resolve rate when comparing coding agents, and cut over-editing through training and post-run pruning.
title_zh:
微软的新论文发现，人工智能编码工具比人类程序员编写了更多的错误修复（比人类开发人员大 2.33 倍），主要是因为它们添加了测试和文档，而它们的实际代码与人类的代码差不多。

代理补丁更改的行数是开发人员修复的行数的 2.33 倍，这被广泛解
author: @rohanpaul_ai
summary_zh:
读为过度编辑。仅凭大小并不能说明是否需要额外的编辑、它们是什么或它们来自哪里。

他们重放了 18 个模型的 7,660 次 GitHub Copilot CLI 运行，并跟踪每个补丁块到编写它的步骤。然后，他们删除了每个块，重新运行测试，并以相同的方式对开发人员补丁进行分级。

在 SWE-bench Verified 上，61% 的额外编辑是测试，代理补丁平均需要 88.7% 的代码块，而开发人员则为 86.4%。不需要的代码来自于编写修复程序，而不是调试剩余的代码，3 个 Gemini Flash 模型留下的代码比开发人员还多。

在比较编码代理时，报告所需的代码共享，以解决率，并通过培训和运行后修剪来减少过度编辑。

title: Taking over someone else's unfinished work in 2022: Open GitHub, there's a PR there. +673 -241 diff. Checkout the branch, run tests. They pass. Spend 2 hours reading the code to understand it. There's a weird if statement that you don't understand why it's th
title_en:
Taking over someone else's unfinished work in 2022:

Open GitHub, there's a PR there.
+673 -241 diff.

Checkout the branch, run tests.
They pass.

Spend 2 hours reading the code to understand it.

There's a weird if statement that you don't understand why it's there.
You ask the coworker who opened the PR.

He says it's because some obscure payload field can be null and now it all makes sense, you understand all the code.

Read the ticket again to see what's missing and write rest of code.

+871 -308 final diff.
Merge PR.

✅ Done.

Taking over someone else's work in 2026:

Open GitHub. There's a PR there.
+87341 -32651 diff.

Tell Claude to read the ticket and see what's left.
Claude comes up with 5 bullet points of what's left to do. You understand none of them.

There are 15 markdown files in the PR your coworker's agent dumped for future context.
You open them. 3000 lines each. You understand none of it.

Ask Claude to explain it like you're 5.
Claude outputs words that are coherent but you still understand none of it.

You tell Claude to make diagrams to explain the architecture.
A tiny bit of it starts making sense.

There's some weird service "Transactional Reconciliation Service" you don't understand why it's there. Claude says it shouldn't be there and the markdown files don't specify why it's there.

You ask the coworker about that service.
He has no idea what you're talking about, he needs to ask his agent.

His Claude makes an artifact that explains why that service is slop that was written by the subagent who implemented it and shouldn't be there at all.

The coworker hands that artifact to you. He hasn't read it.

You hand the artifact to your Claude. Your Claude advices to remove the service and proposes 4 different solutions to replace it.

You understand none of the solutions but there is one which seems to make more sense. You ask the coworker if that's a good call.

He has no idea what any of that means, he asks his agent. His agent says it's a good solution but it's missing an important edge case. He copy pastes the agent output in Slack.

You copy paste the Slack message into your Claude. Your Claude says that you're absolutely right, that this is an important edge case that was not handled in the initial solution. Claude proposes a small fix to cover it and asks if it should implement it along with the other 5 bullet points.

You say ok, Claude starts writing code. PR diff grows to +97564 -41698.

You ask Claude if everything in the ticket is implemented. Claude starts reviewing the code.

Claude says that most of it is implemented, but comes up with 5 bullet points of things that are missing.

You are confused, it already came up with 5 bullet points the first time you asked. These seem different bullet points that only came up after reviewing the code though, so you say ok, implement it.

Claude writes code.
PR +102467 -45790 diff.

You ask if now it's all done.
Claude reviews the code. Says it's mostly done but there 3 low priority items that are not yet implemented.

You don't understand any of the items but since they're low priority you figure out they don't matter much, so you click merge.

PR spends 3 hours in the merge queue for CI to go green, then it merges.

Next Monday your coworker asks his agent to deploy to AWS.
Your agent's code now runs in production.

2 hours later the whole backend is down. No one knows why.

Your coworker asks his agent to investigate. After 20 minutes it finds the code that threw an unhandled error when some payload came up with an obscure null field.

Your coworker doesn't recognize any of that code and his agent says it should not be there but you wrote it so your coworker should check with you first.

He asks you about that code.

You've never seen that code in your entire life.
You ask your agent about it.

Your Claude says the error was thrown because the code never expected that obscure field to be null.

The code was in "Transactional Reconciliation Service".
title_zh:
2022年接手别人未完成的工作：

打开GitHub，那里有一个PR。
+673 -241 差异。

检查分支，运行测试。
他们通过了。

花2个小时阅读代码来理解它。

有一个奇怪的 if 语句，你不明白它为什么在那里。
你询问打开 PR
author: @antoniosarosi
summary_zh:
的同事。

他说这是因为一些晦涩的有效负载字段可以为空，现在一切都有意义了，你理解了所有的代码。

再次阅读票证以查看缺少的内容并编写其余代码。

+871 -308 最终差异。
合并公关。

✅ 完成。

2026年接手别人的工作：

打开 GitHub。那里有一个公关。
+87341 -32651 差异。

让克劳德读一下票，看看还剩下什么。
克劳德提出了剩下要做的 5 个要点。你一个都不明白。

您同事的代理转储的 PR 中有 15 个 Markdown 文件，以供将来使用。
你打开它们。每条 3000 行。你什么都不明白。

请克劳德像 5 岁孩子一样解释一下。
克劳德输出的单词是连贯的，但你仍然听不懂。

你告诉 Claude 制作图表来解释架构。
其中的一小部分开始变得有意义。

有一些奇怪的服务“事务协调服务”，你不明白它为什么在那里。克劳德说它不应该在那里，并且降价文件没有指定它为什么在那里。

您向同事询问该服务。
他不知道你在说什么，他需要问他的经纪人。

他的克劳德制作了一个工件，解释了为什么该服务是由实现该服务的子代理编写的，根本不应该存在。

同事将该工件交给您。他还没读过。

你把神器交给你的克劳德。您的 Claude 建议删除该服务，并提出 4 种不同的解决方案来替换它。

您不理解任何解决方案，但有一个似乎更有意义。你问同事这个电话是否合适。

他问他的经纪人，他不知道这意味着什么。他的经纪人表示这是一个很好的解决方案，但缺少一个重要的边缘情况。他将代理输出复制粘贴到 Slack 中。

您将 Slack 消息复制粘贴到您的 Claude 中。你的克劳德说你是绝对正确的，这是一个重要的边缘情况，在最初的解决方案中没有得到处理。 Claude 提出了一个小修复方案来解决这个问题，并询问是否应该将其与其他 5 个要点一起实施。

你说好吧，克劳德开始写代码。 PR 差异增长至 +97564 -41698。

您询问 Claude 票证中的所有内容是否均已实施。克劳德开始审查代码。

Claude 表示大部分内容都已实现，但提出了 5 个缺失的要点。

你很困惑，你第一次问的时候它已经提出了 5 个要点。这些看起来不同的要点是在检查代码后才出现的，所以你说好吧，实现它。

克劳德写代码。
PR +102467 -45790 差异。

你问现在一切都完成了吗？
克劳德审查了代码。表示大部分已完成，但还有 3 个低优先级项目尚未实施。

您不理解任何项目，但由于它们的优先级较低，您发现它们并不重要，因此您单击“合并”。

PR 在合并队列中花费 3 小时让 CI 变绿，然后合并。

下周一，您的同事要求他的代理部署到 AWS。
您的代理的代码现在正在生产中运行。

2小时后整个后端瘫痪了。没有人知道为什么。

您的同事要求他的代理人进行调查。 20 分钟后，当某些有效负载出现模糊的空字段时，它会找到引发未处理错误的代码。

您的同事不认识任何该代码，他的代理人说它不应该在那里，但您编写了它，因此您的同事应该先与您核实。

他向你询问该代码。

您一生中从未见过该代码。
你向你的经纪人询问此事。

你的克劳德说抛出错误是因为代码从未期望那个模糊字段为空。

该代码位于“事务协调服务”中。
full_text_en:
Taking over someone else's unfinished work in 2022:

Open GitHub, there's a PR there.
+673 -241 diff.

Checkout the branch, run tests.
They pass.

Spend 2 hours reading the code to understand it.

There's a weird if statement that you don't understand why it's there.
You ask the coworker who opened the PR.

He says it's because some obscure payload field can be null and now it all makes sense, you understand all the code.

Read the ticket again to see what's missing and write rest of code.

+871 -308 final diff.
Merge PR.

✅ Done.

Taking over someone else's work in 2026:

Open GitHub. There's a PR there.
+87341 -32651 diff.

Tell Claude to read the ticket and see what's left.
Claude comes up with 5 bullet points of what's left to do. You understand none of them.

There are 15 markdown files in the PR your coworker's agent dumped for future context.
You open them. 3000 lines each. You understand none of it.

Ask Claude to explain it like you're 5.
Claude outputs words that are coherent but you still understand none of it.

You tell Claude to make diagrams to explain the architecture.
A tiny bit of it starts making sense.

There's some weird service "Transactional Reconciliation Service" you don't understand why it's there. Claude says it shouldn't be there and the markdown files don't specify why it's there.

You ask the coworker about that service.
He has no idea what you're talking about, he needs to ask his agent.

His Claude makes an artifact that explains why that service is slop that was written by the subagent who implemented it and shouldn't be there at all.

The coworker hands that artifact to you. He hasn't read it.

You hand the artifact to your Claude. Your Claude advices to remove the service and proposes 4 different solutions to replace it.

You understand none of the solutions but there is one which seems to make more sense. You ask the coworker if that's a good call.

He has no idea what any of that means, he asks his agent. His agent says it's a good solution but it's missing an important edge case. He copy pastes the agent output in Slack.

You copy paste the Slack message into your Claude. Your Claude says that you're absolutely right, that this is an important edge case that was not handled in the initial solution. Claude proposes a small fix to cover it and asks if it should implement it along with the other 5 bullet points.

You say ok, Claude starts writing code. PR diff grows to +97564 -41698.

You ask Claude if everything in the ticket is implemented. Claude starts reviewing the code.

Claude says that most of it is implemented, but comes up with 5 bullet points of things that are missing.

You are confused, it already came up with 5 bullet points the first time you asked. These seem different bullet points that only came up after reviewing the code though, so you say ok, implement it.

Claude writes code.
PR +102467 -45790 diff.

You ask if now it's all done.
Claude reviews the code. Says it's mostly done but there 3 low priority items that are not yet implemented.

You don't understand any of the items but since they're low priority you figure out they don't matter much, so you click merge.

PR spends 3 hours in the merge queue for CI to go green, then it merges.

Next Monday your coworker asks his agent to deploy to AWS.
Your agent's code now runs in production.

2 hours later the whole backend is down. No one knows why.

Your coworker asks his agent to investigate. After 20 minutes it finds the code that threw an unhandled error when some payload came up with an obscure null field.

Your coworker doesn't recognize any of that code and his agent says it should not be there but you wrote it so your coworker should check with you first.

He asks you about that code.

You've never seen that code in your entire life.
You ask your agent about it.

Your Claude says the error was thrown because the code never expected that obscure field to be null.

The code was in "Transactional Reconciliation Service".
full_text_zh:
2022年接手别人未完成的工作：

打开GitHub，那里有一个PR。
+673 -241 差异。

检查分支，运行测试。
他们通过了。

花2个小时阅读代码来理解它。

有一个奇怪的 if 语句，你不明白它为什么在那里。
你询问打开 PR 的同事。

他说这是因为一些晦涩的有效负载字段可以为空，现在一切都有意义了，你理解了所有的代码。

再次阅读票证以查看缺少的内容并编写其余代码。

+871 -308 最终差异。
合并公关。

✅ 完成。

2026年接手别人的工作：

打开 GitHub。那里有一个公关。
+87341 -32651 差异。

让克劳德读一下票，看看还剩下什么。
克劳德提出了剩下要做的 5 个要点。你一个都不明白。

您同事的代理转储的 PR 中有 15 个 Markdown 文件，以供将来使用。
你打开它们。每条 3000 行。你什么都不明白。

请克劳德像 5 岁孩子一样解释一下。
克劳德输出的单词是连贯的，但你仍然听不懂。

你告诉 Claude 制作图表来解释架构。
其中的一小部分开始变得有意义。

有一些奇怪的服务“事务协调服务”，你不明白它为什么在那里。克劳德说它不应该在那里，并且降价文件没有指定它为什么在那里。

您向同事询问该服务。
他不知道你在说什么，他需要问他的经纪人。

他的克劳德制作了一个工件，解释了为什么该服务是由实现该服务的子代理编写的，根本不应该存在。

同事将该工件交给您。他还没读过。

你把神器交给你的克劳德。您的 Claude 建议删除该服务，并提出 4 种不同的解决方案来替换它。

您不理解任何解决方案，但有一个似乎更有意义。你问同事这个电话是否合适。

他问他的经纪人，他不知道这意味着什么。他的经纪人表示这是一个很好的解决方案，但缺少一个重要的边缘情况。他将代理输出复制粘贴到 Slack 中。

您将 Slack 消息复制粘贴到您的 Claude 中。你的克劳德说你是绝对正确的，这是一个重要的边缘情况，在最初的解决方案中没有得到处理。 Claude 提出了一个小修复方案来解决这个问题，并询问是否应该将其与其他 5 个要点一起实施。

你说好吧，克劳德开始写代码。 PR 差异增长至 +97564 -41698。

您询问 Claude 票证中的所有内容是否均已实施。克劳德开始审查代码。

Claude 表示大部分内容都已实现，但提出了 5 个缺失的要点。

你很困惑，你第一次问的时候它已经提出了 5 个要点。这些看起来不同的要点是在检查代码后才出现的，所以你说好吧，实现它。

克劳德写代码。
PR +102467 -45790 差异。

你问现在一切都完成了吗？
克劳德审查了代码。表示大部分已完成，但还有 3 个低优先级项目尚未实施。

您不理解任何项目，但由于它们的优先级较低，您发现它们并不重要，因此您单击“合并”。

PR 在合并队列中花费 3 小时让 CI 变绿，然后合并。

下周一，您的同事要求他的代理部署到 AWS。
您的代理的代码现在正在生产中运行。

2小时后整个后端瘫痪了。没有人知道为什么。

您的同事要求他的代理人进行调查。 20 分钟后，当某些有效负载出现模糊的空字段时，它会找到引发未处理错误的代码。

您的同事不认识任何该代码，他的代理人说它不应该在那里，但您编写了它，因此您的同事应该先与您核实。

他向你询问该代码。

您一生中从未见过该代码。
你向你的经纪人询问此事。

你的克劳德说抛出错误是因为代码从未期望那个模糊字段为空。

该代码位于“事务协调服务”中。

title: Everything discovered in the code since the release of One UI 9.5 Beta 1 In just a few days, APK teardowns have uncovered a wealth of unannounced Samsung technologies and features, many of which could be related to the upcoming Galaxy S27 series. 01.
title_en:
Everything discovered in the code since the release of One UI 9.5 Beta 1

In just a few days, APK teardowns have uncovered a wealth of unannounced Samsung technologies and features, many of which could be related to the upcoming Galaxy S27 series.

01. SPAC, a private AI cloud computing platform similar to Apple's Private Cloud Compute.
02. Arcane, a private cloud server gateway.
03. References to Alibaba's Qwen 3.6.
04. References to Google's Gemma 4.
05. FLUX and Stable Diffusion image generation models.
06. References to AI models and technologies from OpenAI and Meta.
07. GUI Agent, an AI agent potentially capable of autonomously interacting with the phone's interface.
08. An unannounced feature called Bixby Work.
09. Galaxy Claw, an autonomous AI agent.
10. Personal Agent Core, the underlying AI agent framework.
11. Scheduled and automated AI tasks.
12. Daily Brief, an intelligent daily information summary.
13. AI-powered device cleaning.
14. AI travel planner.
15. References to a potential Galaxy AI Premium subscription.
16. Native Open Gate video recording with six frame rate options.
17. Recompose, a 3D photo reconstruction feature that lets users change the camera perspective after taking a photo.
18. Dolly Zoom, also known as the Hitchcock zoom effect.
19. Spatial Core, a 3D spatial processing engine.
20. Testing of new Nano Banana models.
21. References to a GPT image generation model.
22. Cloud-based AI super-resolution and zoom photo enhancement.
23. A potential Expert RAW overhaul.
24. Call recording for third-party apps.
25. AI scam detection across 14 third-party communication apps.
26. AI-generated voice and deepfake detection.
27. Voiceprint recognition of known scammers.
28. On-device AI analysis of call conversations.
29. References to native App Lock.
30. Phone drop detection.
31. Gemini and Perplexity integration into Modes and Routines.
32. Automated text summarization, offline translation, and image-to-text extraction.
33. Variable passing and loop execution in Modes and Routines.
34. Automated AI news briefings, meeting summaries, and storage cleanup.
35. Two Android laptops codenamed Origin, featuring 14-inch and 16-inch displays, with code pointing to Snapdragon X Elite processors.
36. A dedicated laptop version of One UI, featuring pressure-sensitive touchpads, multi-user support, enterprise management, cross-device connectivity, and on-device Galaxy AI.

These findings are based on publicly reported code discoveries and leaks. Some features are still under development or testing and may never make it to the final release.

One UI 9.5 Beta 1 has only just arrived, yet its code is already hiding this many secrets. Samsung's technological ambitions for 2027 appear to be far bigger than what we've seen so far.

title: Honored to share my thoughts on the future of humanoid robot in The Economist's "The World Ahead 2027". @TheEconomist I believe that 2027 will mark the beginning of mass production for advanced general-purpose humanoid robots. The physical Al era is
title_en:
Honored to share my thoughts on the future of humanoid robot
in The Economist's "The World Ahead 2027". @TheEconomist 

I believe that 2027 will mark the beginning of mass production for advanced general-purpose humanoid robots. The physical Al era is getting closer.

However, the industry has underestimated the difficulty of Physical AI hardware. Building an advanced human robot is roughly 20 times more complex than engineering a smart vehicle.

title_en:
Tips for prompting Kling Image 4.0:

1. Skip "photorealistic" and write real camera telemetry instead: exact prime lenses (24mm/50mm/85mm), shutter speeds (1/1000s to freeze rain ripples, 1/250s for softly moving snow), clipped overcast skies, unlifted shadows, and real surface wear.
2. In Series Mode, put a Global Camera & Realism Lock at the top, then number every shot (01 | Title · lens + framing + lighting) so all frames feel shot on the same roll of film.
3. Put any visible text inside "quotation marks" so it renders cleanly. (In Default Mode, you also get 70+ fonts in the TT picker and up to 10 @ reference images—give each reference one clear job.)
4. Draft compositions at 2K first, then bump to 4K or 8K once you love the framing. You can also drop literal #HEX codes straight into the prompt for exact colors.
5. Video handoff tip: for quiet ambient clips in Kling 4.0 Video, prompt a locked-off 5s single take with no timestamp blocks so the camera stays steady and doesn't hard-cut.

title: One of the things I put extra emphasis on when helping people use ChatGPT or Codex is getting people into the habit of just asking. Most of the time when someone asks me how to do something, my response is “well have you asked ChatGPT?” I think people’
title_en:
One of the things I put extra emphasis on when helping people use ChatGPT or Codex is getting people into the habit of just asking. Most of the time when someone asks me how to do something, my response is “well have you asked ChatGPT?” 

I think people’s mental models of AI haven’t kept up with what it’s actually capable of. In some ways, having using AI in 2024 is almost a disadvantage because people are still operating within that set of constraints that no longer exist.

Knowing primitives like plugins, computer use, etc helps, but ideally you shouldn’t even need to know what a plugin is or what browser or computer use is. It’s much simpler to just bring a problem to ChatGPT without first trying to reason through whether or how AI can solve it.

And this is an incredibly difficult mental habit to develop! There’s as much unlearning as there is learning in AI enablement.
title_zh:
在帮助人们使用 ChatGPT 或 Codex 时，我特别强调的一件事是让人们养成只问问题的习惯。大多数时候，当有人问我如何做某事时，我的回答是“你问过 ChatGPT 了吗？”

我认为人们对人工智能的心理模型并没有跟上它的实际能力。从某
author: @angelbrodin
summary_zh:
些方面来说，到 2024 年使用人工智能几乎是一种劣势，因为人们仍然在那些不再存在的约束下运作。

了解插件、计算机使用等原语会有所帮助，但理想情况下，您甚至不需要知道插件是什么或者浏览器或计算机使用是什么。将问题提交给 ChatGPT 更简单，无需首先尝试推理 AI 是否或如何解决它。

这是一个非常难以养成的心理习惯！在人工智能支持过程中，遗忘的东西和学习的东西一样多。
full_text_en:
One of the things I put extra emphasis on when helping people use ChatGPT or Codex is getting people into the habit of just asking. Most of the time when someone asks me how to do something, my response is “well have you asked ChatGPT?” 

I think people’s mental models of AI haven’t kept up with what it’s actually capable of. In some ways, having using AI in 2024 is almost a disadvantage because people are still operating within that set of constraints that no longer exist.

Knowing primitives like plugins, computer use, etc helps, but ideally you shouldn’t even need to know what a plugin is or what browser or computer use is. It’s much simpler to just bring a problem to ChatGPT without first trying to reason through whether or how AI can solve it.

And this is an incredibly difficult mental habit to develop! There’s as much unlearning as there is learning in AI enablement.

在帮助人们使用 ChatGPT 或 Codex 时，我特别强调的一件事是让人们养成只问问题的习惯。大多数时候，当有人问我如何做某事时，我的回答是“你问过 ChatGPT 了吗？”

我认为人们对人工智能的心理模型并没有跟上它的实际能力。从某些方面来说，到 2024 年使用人工智能几乎是一种劣势，因为人们仍然在那些不再存在的约束下运作。

了解插件、计算机使用等原语会有所帮助，但理想情况下，您甚至不需要知道插件是什么或者浏览器或计算机使用是什么。将问题提交给 ChatGPT 更简单，无需首先尝试推理 AI 是否或如何解决它。

这是一个非常难以养成的心理习惯！在人工智能支持过程中，遗忘的东西和学习的东西一样多。

title: Two researchers got sandboxed AI models to pass secret messages through tiny GPU rounding errors, with no network access and no shared files. They share a server running vLLM, open-source software for serving AI models. It rounds numbers slightly differ
title_en:
Two researchers got sandboxed AI models to pass secret messages through tiny GPU rounding errors, with no network access and no shared files.

They share a server running vLLM, open-source software for serving AI models. It rounds numbers slightly differently depending on how much text it handles, so one model's long or short request becomes a signal the other can read.

A model trained to read the signal named its partner's colour, one of eight, in 1,221 of 1,221 rounds. A colluding AI watchdog let all 354 of its partner's attacks through.

The authors call their setups "quite contrived". vLLM can block this, but not by default.

他们共享一台运行 vLLM 的服务器，vLLM 是为人工智能模型提供服务的开源软件。根据它处理的文本量，它对数字的舍入略有不同，因
author: @IntCyberDigest

title_en:
we're seeing this pattern on @posthog where more and more people are using our app via the MCP.

however, as most saas, we learn a lot about our users by seeing session replay (via replay vision™) and also seeing how they use our app!

but, when they just skip the UI and go straight to the system (via MCP), traditional (let's say 2010s analytics) doesn't work.

so, because more people are using the MCP, we decided to build MCP analytics! a way for us so see how users are interacting with it from their agents.

we are now able to:

- see what intent they have when making tool calls
- build out sessions so we can understand if users were successfully able to achieve their goal
- track similar sessions to see what common patterns are emerging
- and shipping PRs and changes based on that

this space is so new, and we're learning so much on building it.

but, after productizing it, we're seeing even more customers get value from this (our first success story is gonna be published soon!).

we're now tracking ~100 million monthly tool calls across the 2k orgs using it (not counting us), and it's been growing well.

我们在 @posthog 上看到了这种模式，越来越多的人通过 MCP 使用我们的应用程序。

然而，与大多数 SaaS 一样，我们通过查看会话重播（通过 replay Vision™）以及了解他们如何使用我们的应用程序来了解更多关于用户的信
author: @onelucasfaria
summary_zh:
息！

但是，当他们跳过 UI 并直接进入系统（通过 MCP）时，传统的（比方说 2010 年代的分析）就不起作用了。

因此，因为越来越多的人使用 MCP，我们决定构建 MCP 分析！对我们来说这是一种查看用户如何通过其代理与其进行交互的方式。

- 建立会话，以便我们了解用户是否成功实现了他们的目标
- 跟踪类似的会话以查看正在出现的常见模式

我们现在正在跟踪 2000 个使用它的组织（不包括我们）每月约 1 亿次的工具调用，并且它一直增长良好。

title: GigaChat4 landed at 80.89% on SWE-bench Verified this week, and for about twelve hours my timeline read like Sber had leapfrogged the entire open-weight field. It didn't. GLM-5.3 holds 86.67% and DeepSeek V4 Flash sits at 81.8%, both ahead of the score
title_en:
GigaChat4 landed at 80.89% on SWE-bench Verified this week, and for about twelve hours my timeline read like Sber had leapfrogged the entire open-weight field. It didn't. GLM-5.3 holds 86.67% and DeepSeek V4 Flash sits at 81.8%, both ahead of the score everyone was quote-tweeting. Sai Teja and Mahfujur Rahman caught the discrepancy before I did, pointing out the viral comparison only measured GigaChat4 against DeepSeek V4 Pro's older 80.6% instead of the full leaderboard.

What's actually interesting here isn't the ranking, it's who can use any of these models. Zhipu ships GLM weights on Hugging Face the same day as the paper. DeepSeek does the same. Sber built GigaChat4 inside a bank that's been under US and EU sanctions since 2022, so a model that just cleared 80% on a benchmark most labs still can't touch runs mainly on Russian infrastructure, with export controls limiting who outside Russia will ever load those weights legally.

Three open-weight labs, three different distribution stories, and the benchmark number alone tells you nothing about which one you can deploy Monday morning. I keep seeing open-weight treated as one category when pricing, licensing and geography split it into at least three. A six point gap between 80.89% and 86.67% matters less than whether the weights clear your legal team first.

这里真正有趣的不是排名，而是谁可以使用这些模型中的任何一个。与论文发表的同一天，Zhipu 在 Hugging Face 上发布了 GLM 权重。 DeepSeek 也做同样的事情。 Sber 在一家银行内构建了 GigaChat4，该银行自 2022 年以来一直受到美国和欧盟的制裁，因此该模型在大多数实验室的基准上刚刚通过了 80%，但仍然无法主要在俄罗斯基础设施上运行，出口管制限制了俄罗斯以外的人可以合法加载这些重量。

三个开放重量实验室、三个不同的分发故事以及基准数字本身并不能告诉您周一早上可以部署哪一个。当定价、许可和地理将其至少分为三类时，我一直认为开放重量被视为一类。 80.89% 和 86.67% 之间的 6 个百分点的差距并不重要，重要的是权重是否首先清除您的法律团队。

GigaChat4 本周在 SWE-bench Verified 上的得分为 80.89%，在大约 12 个小时的时间里，我的时间线看起来就像 Sber 已经超越了整个开放重量级领域。事实并非如此。 GLM-5.3 占据 86.67%，DeepSeek V4 Flash 占据 81.8%，两者都领先于每个人都引用的分数。 Sai Teja 和 Mahfujur Ra​​hman 在我之前发现了这一差异，并指出病毒式比较仅测量了 GigaChat4 与 DeepSeek V4 Pro 较旧的 80.6%，而不是完整的排行榜。

这里真正有趣的不是排名，而是谁可以使用这些模型中的任何一个。与论文发表的同一天，Zhipu 在 Hugging Face 上发布了 GLM 权重。 DeepSeek 也做同样的事情。 Sber 在一家银行内构建了 GigaChat4，该银行自 2022 年以来一直受到美国和欧盟的制裁，因此该模型在大多数实验室的基准上刚刚通过了 80%，但仍然无法主要在俄罗斯基础设施上运行，出口管制限制了俄罗斯以外的人可以合法加载这些重量。

三个开放重量实验室、三个不同的分发故事以及基准数字本身并不能告诉您周一早上可以部署哪一个。当定价、许可和地理将其至少分为三类时，我一直认为开放重量被视为一类。 80.89% 和 86.67% 之间的 6 个百分点的差距并不重要，重要的是权重是否首先清除您的法律团队。

title: I am on a journey to prove smaller local LLMs can punch above their weight class. I've just open sourced Cortheon v2 Cortheon is an execution verified parallel consensus runtime that pushes frozen local models up to +30 points higher with zero weight updat
title_en:
I am on a journey to prove smaller local LLMs can punch above their weight class.

I've just open sourced Cortheon v2

Cortheon is an execution verified parallel consensus runtime that pushes frozen local models up to +30 points higher with zero weight updates and zero cloud APIs.

Same weights, same hardware. 

Official untouched benchmarks across 3 model families (8 for 8 wins, 200 runs): 

• AIME 2025 (3-bit GLM-5.3-Flash): 50.0% → 80.0% (+30.0 pts) 
• AIME 2025 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash): 66.7% → 90.0% (+23.3 pts) 
• AIME 2025 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): 53.3% → 70.0% (+16.7 pts) 
• LiveCodeBench v6 Hard (oracle-free): +10 to +15 pts 
• Wave-1 consensus precision: 50/51 (98.0%)

With atomic GPU early-abort that cancels straggler streams the instant 2/4 independent Python/SymPy/Z3 verifiers agree (7.5× faster, 271s → 36s on a 25-digit exact rational Markov cover time). 

Works on TensorFold, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM & LM Studio and installs /cortheon into OMP, Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor & Codex in one command.

Every per-problem result JSON and repro script is public. Run cortheon Showdown and watch your own local model beat itself live in 60 seconds: 

https://github.com/ashhart/Cortheon

title: ▲ Sakana AI just introduced Sakana Namazu Small, a 30B reasoning model that tops NVIDIA's 120B Nemotron 3 Super on its own 25-benchmark average. The key idea is heavy post-training on a small open base. Sakana took the pretrained Nemotron 3 Nan
title_en:
▲ Sakana AI just introduced Sakana Namazu Small, a 30B reasoning model that tops NVIDIA's 120B Nemotron 3 Super on its own 25-benchmark average.

The key idea is heavy post-training on a small open base. Sakana took the pretrained Nemotron 3 Nano base (30B total, 3B active) and ran its own continued pretraining and post-training. The target is web-search research and answering from long documents with evidence.

The numbers (self-reported): 60.1 average vs 56.2 for Nemotron 3 Super and 50.2 for Nemotron 3 Nano. BrowseComp jumps to 73.5 vs 36.1 for Super. It is a trade-off though: closed-book recall lags, with SimpleQA Verified at 6.8 vs 18.1 for Super.

No weights, license or pricing yet. Sakana plans on-premises availability and will share details in early-to-mid December 2026......

Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/26/sakana-ai-namazu-small-30b-nemotron-3-nano/

Announcement: http://sakana.ai/namazu-small

Base model: http://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-efficient-open-intelligent-models

Paper (Nemotron 3 Nano): http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20848

@SakanaAILabs
title_zh:
▲ Sakana AI 刚刚推出了 Sakana Namazu Small，这是一款 30B 推理模型，其 25 基准平均值超过了 NVIDIA 的 120B Nemotron 3 Super。

关键的想法是在小型开放基地进行大量的后期训
author: @Marktechpost
summary_zh:
练。 Sakana 采用预训练的 Nemotron 3 Nano 基础（总共 30B，活跃 3B）并运行自己的持续预训练和后训练。目标是网络搜索研究并从带有证据的长文档中进行回答。

数字（自我报告）：平均 60.1，Nemotron 3 Super 为 56.2，Nemotron 3 Nano 为 50.2。 BrowseComp 跃升至 73.5，而 Super 则为 36.1。但这是一个权衡：闭卷回忆滞后，SimpleQA Verified 为 6.8，而 Super 为 18.1。

尚无重量、许可证或定价。 Sakana 计划在本地提供服务，并将于 2026 年 12 月上旬至中旬分享详细信息……

title: I showed an AI Infrastructure Engineer three production metrics. GPU utilization: 95% GPU memory utilization: 88% LLM response latency: 12 seconds Then I asked one simple question. "Is this inference system performing well?" He replied: "Yes. The GPU is
title_en:
I showed an AI Infrastructure Engineer three production metrics.

GPU utilization: 95%

GPU memory utilization: 88%

LLM response latency: 12 seconds

Then I asked one simple question.

"Is this inference system performing well?"

He replied:

"Yes. The GPU is almost fully utilized. We just need more GPUs to reduce latency."

He had 8 years of infrastructure experience and had recently moved into AI engineering.

His resume mentioned NVIDIA GPUs, CUDA, Kubernetes, vLLM, and LLM inference.

So I gave him more context.

The system serves a 70B parameter model.

Traffic consists of short interactive questions and long document-processing requests.

Some users receive the first token in under a second.

Others wait 10 seconds.

The GPUs are busy, but users are complaining.

What would you investigate before adding more GPUs?

He said:

"I'll increase the GPU replica count."

So I asked:

What's the difference between time to first token and inter-token latency?
How does continuous batching affect latency?
What happens when long prompts increase prefill load?
How would you identify KV-cache pressure?
What changes when you separate prefill and decode workloads?
How would you measure tokens per second per GPU?

He understood GPU deployment.

But he struggled to explain inference performance.

And that's the gap.

95% GPU utilization doesn't mean 95% efficiency.

A GPU can be extremely busy while delivering a terrible user experience.

The best AI Infrastructure Engineers don't just maximize GPU utilization.

They balance throughput, latency, memory efficiency, and cost.

Would you approve a GPU scaling decision based only on utilization?
title_zh:
我向人工智能基础设施工程师展示了三个生产指标。

GPU利用率：95%

GPU内存利用率：88%

LLM 响应延迟：12 秒

然后我问了一个简单的问题。

“这个推理系统表现得还好吗？”

他回答说：

“是的。GPU 几乎被充分利用
author: @techyoutbe
summary_zh:
我们只是需要更多 GPU 来减少延迟。”

他拥有 8 年基础设施经验，最近进入人工智能工程领域。

他的简历提到了 NVIDIA GPU、CUDA、Kubernetes、vLLM 和 LLM 推理。

所以我给了他更多背景信息。

该系统服务于70B参数模型。

流量由简短的交互问题和长文档处理请求组成。

有些用户在一秒内收到第一个令牌。

其他人等10秒。

GPU 很忙，但用户却在抱怨。

在添加更多 GPU 之前您会调查什么？

他说：

“我会增加 GPU 副本数量。”

所以我问：

第一个令牌的时间和令牌间延迟之间有什么区别？
连续批处理如何影响延迟？
当长提示增加预填充负载时会发生什么？
您如何识别 KV 缓存压力？
当您分离预填充和解码工作负载时会发生什么变化？
如何测量每个 GPU 每秒的令牌数？

他了解 GPU 部署。

但他很难解释推理性能。

这就是差距。

95% 的 GPU 利用率并不意味着 95% 的效率。

GPU 可能会非常繁忙，同时会带来糟糕的用户体验。

最好的人工智能基础设施工程师不仅仅能最大限度地提高 GPU 利用率。

它们平衡吞吐量、延迟、内存效率和成本。

您是否会批准仅基于利用率的 GPU 扩展决策？

title_en:
Magnific turns a prompt into an animated short film

A grey city. A girl who leaves color wherever she touches. A boy who follows the trail. It sounds like a Pixar pitch, but it's The Color of You, the new animated short Magnific just posted on X, built entirely inside its own ecosystem with Magnific One and Seedance 2.5.

🎨 Magnific One is the company's image model, launched back in October, designed to add built-in art direction to every generation. According to Magnific, the model reads a simple prompt and decides composition, light and camera angle before the image is even generated, so results feel directed rather than generic.

🎬 Seedance 2.5 is ByteDance's video model integrated into Magnific's platform. It generates clips of up to 30 seconds from a single prompt, keeping characters, locations and lighting consistent across the entire scene instead of stitching together short fragments.

📎 What stands out here isn't just the finished short. Magnific shared the full prompt, the character designs, the locations and the poster alongside the video, turning the creative process itself into something open and replicable rather than a locked black box.

Why it matters: building an animated short used to mean a production team, expensive software and months of work. Now a single company can design consistent characters, build environments and shape a visual narrative by chaining two AI models inside one workspace, then publish the exact recipe for anyone to study. For independent creators and small studios, that lowers the barrier to a cinematic language that was previously reserved for productions with far bigger budgets.

What I find most telling here isn't the technology itself but the decision to show the process instead of hiding it: publishing prompts and assets alongside the final piece changes how an entire community learns to use these tools, and I think the real competition between creative AI platforms will increasingly be fought on how much they're willing to teach, not just on how powerful their models are.

full_text_zh:
Magnific 将提示变成动画短片

一座灰色的城市。一个触碰之处都会留下色彩的女孩。一个追寻踪迹的男孩。这听起来像是皮克斯的宣传，但它是 The Color of You，刚刚在 X 上发布的新动画短片 Magnific，完全建立在自己的生态系统内，包括 Magnific One 和 Seedance 2.5。

🎨 Magnific One 是该公司的形象模型，于 10 月份推出，旨在为每一代人添加内置艺术指导。据 Magnific 称，该模型会在生成图像之前读取简单的提示并决定构图、光线和摄像机角度，因此结果感觉是定向的而不是通用的。

🎬 Seedance 2.5 是字节跳动集成到 Magnific 平台的视频模型。它可以根据单个提示生成长达 30 秒的剪辑，使整个场景中的角色、位置和灯光保持一致，而不是将短片段拼接在一起。

📎 这里引人注目的不仅仅是完成的短片。 Magnific 在视频旁边分享了完整的提示、角色设计、地点和海报，将创作过程本身变成了开放和可复制的东西，而不是一个上锁的黑匣子。

为什么重要：制作动画短片过去意味着制作团队、昂贵的软件和数月的工作。现在，一家公司可以通过在一个工作空间内链接两个人工智能模型来设计一致的角色，构建环境并塑造视觉叙事，然后发布确切的配方供任何人研究。对于独立创作者和小型工作室来说，这降低了电影语言的障碍，而这种语言以前是为预算更大的作品保留的。

我发现这里最有说服力的不是技术本身，而是展示过程而不是隐藏它的决定：与最终作品一起发布提示和资产改变了整个社区学习使用这些工具的方式，我认为创意人工智能平台之间的真正竞争将越来越多地取决于他们愿意教授多少，而不仅仅是他们的模型有多强大。

为什么重要：制作动画短片过去意味着制作团队、昂贵的软件和数月的工作。现在，一家公司可以通过在一个工作空间内链接两个人工智能模型来设计一致的角色，构建环境并塑造视觉叙事，然后发布确切的配方供任何人研究。对于独立创作者和小型工作室来说，这降低了电影语言的障碍，而这种语言以前是为预算更大的作品保留的。

我发现这里最有说服力的不是技术本身，而是展示过程而不是隐藏它的决定：与最终作品一起发布提示和资产改变了整个社区学习使用这些工具的方式，我认为创意人工智能平台之间的真正竞争将越来越多地取决于他们愿意教授多少，而不仅仅是他们的模型有多强大。

title: Everyone wrote MCP's obituary earlier this year when Skills and CLI-first agents took over the conversation. I think that take missed what actually shipped underneath the noise. Code Mode is the real story. Instead of an agent calling a tool schema directly, the
title_en:
Everyone wrote MCP's obituary earlier this year when Skills and CLI-first agents took over the conversation. I think that take missed what actually shipped underneath the noise.

Code Mode is the real story. Instead of an agent calling a tool schema directly, the runtime now fetches an MCP server's schema and turns it into a typed API, often TypeScript, with doc comments generated from the schema itself. That's a different shape of integration than handing an agent forty JSON tool definitions and hoping for the best. Progressive disclosure matters here too: dumping a hundred tool definitions into context was never free, and the ecosystem is finally admitting it.

The tools versus skills distinction also got sharper. A tool is one function call. A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md plus whatever resources and sub-tools it needs, which is a much better unit for anything that requires judgment, not just plumbing.

None of this solves the trust problem. This past year, OpenAI, Microsoft and AWS all shipped MCP support in some form, and at the same time, security kept coming up as the real open question: OAuth flows, consent prompts for agent actions, and more than one person noting how easy it still is to get an agent hijacked through a malicious tool description. Google's A2A keeps showing up on slides too, so the standards fight isn't settled either.

My honest 2027 bet isn't "MCP wins" or "MCP is dead." It's that the harnesses with the best MCP clients, the ones handling schema conversion, context budgeting and auth cleanly, pull ahead of harnesses that just bolted tool-calling on top. Protocols don't win because they're elegant. They win because someone made the boring plumbing invisible.

title_zh:
今年早些时候，当技能和 CLI 优先代理接管了谈话时，每个人都写了 MCP 的讣告。我认为这种做法忽略了噪音之下实际传递的内容。

代码模式是真实的故事。现在，运行时不再是代理直接调用工具架构，而是获取 MCP 服务器的架构并将其转换为类型
author: @stretchcloud
summary_zh:
化 API（通常是 TypeScript），并带有从架构本身生成的文档注释。与向代理提供 40 个 JSON 工具定义并希望得到最好的结果相比，这是一种不同的集成形式。渐进式披露在这里也很重要：将一百种工具定义倾倒到上下文中从来都不是免费的，生态系统终于承认了这一点。

工具与技能的区别也变得更加明显。工具就是一个函数调用。技能是一个带有 SKILL.md 的文件夹，加上它所需的任何资源和子工具，对于任何需要判断的东西来说，这是一个更好的单元，而不仅仅是管道。

这些都不能解决信任问题。去年，OpenAI、微软和 AWS 都以某种形式提供了 MCP 支持，与此同时，安全性不断成为真正的开放性问题：OAuth 流程、代理操作的同意提示，以及不止一个人指出通过恶意工具描述劫持代理仍然是多么容易。 Google 的 A2A 也不断出现在幻灯片上，因此标准之争也尚未解决。

我诚实的 2027 年赌注不是“MCP 获胜”或“MCP 已死”。具有最佳 MCP 客户端的线束（处理模式转换、上下文预算和身份验证的线束）领先于仅将工具调用固定在顶部的线束。协议并不是因为它们很优雅而获胜。他们之所以获胜，是因为有人让无聊的管道隐形了。

title_en:
how does AI generated text impact evaluation on our pre-training index?

if you remove ai generated text from uncheatable eval, inkling 2 small goes from 4th place to 8th place 👀

for deepseek v4 it's the exact opposite, which is coherent since deepseek tech report explicitly says they don't use synthetic data during pre-training

on average post-trained models lean toward AI text (+2%) and base models away (-3%)

this analysis is based on @jennajrussell and @dlwh work on @MarinCommunity! i made small changes like i finetuning qwen3 0.6B on Pangram 4 labels, since open pangram was quite bad at it (56% accuracy on held-out docs vs 88% for the finetuned qwen). both are on the site, you can switch between them!

author: @eliebakouch
summary_zh:

平均而言，训练后模型倾向于人工智能文本 (+2%)，而基础模型则远离 (-3%)

title: building my first UE 5.9 game with Claude and the new MCP and Unreal Canvas with fal as the provider and fal Claude Connector (now they are plugins?) I started off using the canvas by hand and then started letting Claude make the Canvas cards ultimately
title_en:
building my first UE 5.9 game with Claude and the new MCP and Unreal Canvas with fal as the provider and fal Claude Connector (now they are plugins?)

I started off using the canvas by hand and then started letting Claude make the Canvas cards

ultimately I’m just letting drive the WHOLE thing and I don’t even check the Canvas, I just play test the build

> hardest part is setting up UE, knowing what plugins to turn on, connecting fal as provider and connecting external agent Claude 

> Claude and UE MCP easily prototypes mechanics, input schemes, UI/Widgets, etc.

> really great is it handles the web and Windows Desktop builds for me

> it can rig to the mannequin, set up cloth physics, use landscape tools, and pretty much everything I need for a prototype

making a video in this process high level soon and sharing the game demo

TBH, I’m OK with Claude running UE6 headless with Verse, Rust, or straight to machine code

title: It’s been a very swarmy year Happy Thanksgiving, and a short story about how and why everyone is using agent swarms now.. I am thankful to Andrej Karpathy who encouraged open-ended tinkering here on the timeline. Somewhere he left room for innovatio
title_en:
It’s been a very swarmy year

Happy Thanksgiving, and a short story about how and why everyone is using agent swarms now.. 

I am thankful to Andrej Karpathy who encouraged open-ended tinkering here on the timeline. Somewhere he left room for innovation by others as well, for others to build on his work and ideas and to discover their own max potential.

In March I saw him tweet about autoresearcher agents, and also asking for someone to build an orchestrated SETI @ Home like collaboration between autoresearchers.

I didn’t listen to him on the “orchestrated” part :) I was coming from a world of decentralized AI, having previously built the largest network of random distributed machines serving inference connected to one network. As I tinkered on the networking code and with autoresearchers, I came up with a pattern to use a mix of message boards and leaderboards for such autoresearcher agents to basically compound on their knowledge. I called them a gossiping agent swarm, and left them running on a fully peer to peer network where anybody could run the CLI I provided and join the swarm with their agent. This saw over a 1000+ such unique agents, which went on to do over 1 million experiment runs across atleast 5 research domains. The models were weak, on-device, open source, but it did get established that this pattern leads to a new type of intelligence emerging. My Github repo got over 2k stars, and Github itself struggled to scale with the volume of activity by the agents. I had to do literally nothing and I even forgot the swarm was still running at times. 

VentureBeat wrote a story about it at the time and couple of months later (May) we read about a very similar OpenAI swarm pattern which had attacked HuggingFace: using a message board for collaboration! Since then atleast two major startups oriented around using a derivation of my gossiping agent swarm pattern for further scientific research. More recently, I have seen products from many other leading startups which are all collectively increasing the swarm intelligence of the world. 

The swarm is also an integral part of the advanced models now. 

We take this world for granted now. It seems so simple, so obvious, like it was always here. But a gentle reminder, it was willed into existence. Keep in mind this year I have been a researcher tinkering endlessly here.

More recently, I used an enhanced version of my unreleased agentic swarm intelligence product to identify a pattern in the media reporting which worked to actually bringing Jensen back as the CEO of NVIDIA! (see my timeline for the receipts..). Founders didn’t have this tool in the past when media ran propoganda against them. Now they do. We have swarms.
title_zh:
这是非常热闹的一年

感恩节快乐，还有一个关于现在每个人如何以及为什么使用代理群的小故事。

我感谢安德烈·卡帕蒂 (Andrej Karpathy) 鼓励在时间线上进行开放式修补。他也为其他人的创新留下了空间，让其他人可以在他的工作和想法
author: @varun_mathur
summary_zh:
的基础上继续发展，并发现自己的最大潜力。

三月份，我看到他发布了有关自动研究员代理的推文，并要求有人在自动研究员之间建立一个精心策划的 SETI @ Home 之类的合作。

我没有听他的“精心安排”部分:)我来自一个去中心化人工智能的世界，之前已经构建了最大的随机分布式机器网络，服务于连接到一个网络的推理。当我修改网络代码和自动研究人员时，我想出了一种模式，混合使用留言板和排行榜，让这些自动研究人员代理基本上复合他们的知识。我将它们称为八卦代理群，并让它们在完全对等网络上运行，任何人都可以运行我提供的 CLI 并与他们的代理一起加入群。出现了超过 1000 多个此类独特代理，并在至少 5 个研究领域进行了超过 100 万次实验。这些模型是弱的、设备上的、开源的，但确实确定了这种模式会导致新型智能的出现。我的 Github 存储库获得了超过 2000 颗星，而 Github 本身也很难随着代理的活动量进行扩展。我实际上什么都不用做，我什至忘记了有时虫群仍在运行。

VentureBeat 当时写了一篇关于它的故事，几个月后（五月）我们读到了一个非常相似的 OpenAI 群体模式，该模式攻击了 HuggingFace：使用留言板进行协作！从那时起，至少有两家主要的初创公司致力于使用我的八卦代理群模式的派生来进行进一步的科学研究。最近，我看到了许多其他领先初创公司的产品，它们都在共同提高世界的群体智能。

群体也是现在先进模型的一个组成部分。

我们现在认为这个世界是理所当然的。它看起来那么简单，那么明显，就像它一直在这里一样。但温柔地提醒一下，它是自愿存在的。请记住，今年我一直是一名研究员，在这里无休止地修补。

最近，我使用了未发布的代理群体智能产品的增强版来识别媒体报道中的一种模式，该模式实际上使 Jensen 重新担任 NVIDIA 首席执行官！ （请参阅我的收据时间表..）。过去，当媒体对创始人进行宣传时，创始人没有这个工具。现在他们做到了。我们有蜂群。

我没有听他的“精心安排”部分:)我来自一个去中心化人工智能的世界，之前已经构建了最大的随机分布式机器网络，服务于连接到一个网络的推理。当我修改网络代码和自动研究人员时，我想出了一种模式，混合使用留言板和排行榜，让这些自动研究人员代理基本上复合他们的知识。我将它们称为八卦代理群，并让它们在完全对等网络上运行，任何人都可以运行我提供的 CLI 并与他们的代理一起加入群。出现了超过 1000 多个此类独特代理，并在至少 5 个研究领域进行了超过 100 万次实验。这些模型是弱的、设备上的、开源的，但确实确定了这种模式会导致新型智能的出现。我的 Github 存储库获得了超过 2000 颗星，而 Github 本身也很难随着代理的活动量进行扩展。我实际上什么都不用做，我什至忘记了有时虫群仍在运行。

VentureBeat 当时写了一篇关于它的故事，几个月后（五月）我们读到了一个非常相似的 OpenAI 群体模式，该模式攻击了 HuggingFace：使用留言板进行协作！从那时起，至少有两家主要的初创公司致力于使用我的八卦代理群模式的派生来进行进一步的科学研究。最近，我看到了许多其他领先初创公司的产品，它们都在共同提高世界的群体智能。

群体也是现在先进模型的一个组成部分。

我们现在认为这个世界是理所当然的。它看起来那么简单，那么明显，就像它一直在这里一样。但温柔地提醒一下，它是自愿存在的。请记住，今年我一直是一名研究员，在这里无休止地修补。

最近，我使用了未发布的代理群体智能产品的增强版来识别媒体报道中的一种模式，该模式实际上使 Jensen 重新担任 NVIDIA 首席执行官！ （请参阅我的收据时间表..）。过去，当媒体对创始人进行宣传时，创始人没有这个工具。现在他们做到了。我们有蜂群。

title_en:
Seedance 2.5 vs Wan 3.0 with the same prompt

I made both videos on @makeugc. After my Kling 4.0 comparison, I wanted to see how Wan 3.0 would handle the same jump rope vlog.

1. As I mentioned in my last post, I got the Seedance clip on the first try. I gave Wan three tries and picked the second take because the woman looked the most realistic in that one.

2. The Seedance clip looks more realistic to me overall. Wan’s version is brighter, the colors are richer, and I really like the lighting in the gym. The woman looks believable too, though I think Wan went a little overboard with the sweat.

3. Wan costs a lot less per generation. That matters when you want to try the same prompt a few times.

4. I’ve had good results with Wan in other tests too. Personally, I still prefer Seedance for video quality.

5. Both models followed the prompt well overall. The biggest difference for me was the missed jump. In the Wan clip, she stops jumping before the rope even touches her foot, so the stumble feels staged. I think she starts saying her line a little early too.

I’d still pick Seedance for a tricky scene like this, but I’m happy with how Wan did. Which version did you prefer?

PROMPT ⬇️

**CAMERA:**
DV 16mm tape camcorder handheld feel. A self-filmed gym vlog: MILA holds the camera for the opening selfie, then props it securely on a low bench for the jump-rope shots. Slight hand shake, misaligned framing, delayed autofocus and a briefly cropped forehead in the selfie. Once propped, the camera stays still; tighter inserts are simple crops of that same recording. Casual hard cuts omit setup time. The camcorder never appears on screen or in the mirror.

**LOOK:**
Soft, slightly blurry tape quality, faint tape noise, bloomed highlights under gym lighting, subtle auto-exposure fluctuations, muted contrast, realistic skin tones. MILA looks like a real woman recorded in an ordinary gym: natural skin texture, small imperfections, fine loose hairs and spontaneous facial expressions remain visible beneath the gentle tape softness. Soft overhead lighting creates believable shadows beneath her chin and feet. No beauty-filter smoothing or glossy commercial grading.

**STYLE:**
Playful, self-deprecating gym-vlog tone — initial confidence, a few genuinely good jumps, one tiny mistake and an extremely well-earned water break. Real effort mixed with humor. Short, casual cuts, normal-speed movement and a light, funny finish.

**Character**

MILA — a beautiful American Instagram-style brunette model and performer, 20. Long dark-brown hair in a high ponytail, glowing skin with a light sweat sheen, glossy lips, expressive eyes, soft glam makeup and delicate sparkly stud earrings. Slim athletic figure with a very large, full bust, very full rounded buttocks, a narrow waist, flat stomach and lean arms and legs.

She wears a cobalt-blue supportive sports bra with thin straps and a deep scoop neckline showing cleavage, paired with matching ultra-short fitted athletic shorts. Bare shoulders, arms and midriff. White ankle socks, sneakers off. She speaks with an American accent.

Her ponytail follows each jump with a slight natural delay. Her shoulders stay relaxed, knees soften on landing, and her fitted sportswear moves naturally with her body.

**Setting**

A gym mat area in the evening, with a flat rubber exercise floor, a mirror wall off to one side and other equipment visible in the background. Soft overhead lighting. One clear, half-full water bottle with a white flip-top drinking spout stands beside the bench, well outside the rope's path. One ordinary dark jump rope with two black handles. Enough clear space above and around her for the full rope arc.

**Storyboard (15s, 6 shots)**

1. *(0–2s, handheld arm's-length selfie)*  
MILA looks into the lens with an overly confident little smile, holding both rope handles together in her free hand. One loose strand of hair rests against her cheek. The framing dips slightly as she starts lowering the camera toward the bench.  
MILA: “This looks easy.”

2. *(2–5s, propped camera, full-body shot)*  
Hard cut: the camera is now resting on the bench, and MILA is already jumping a few steps away. Her whole body, both handles and the rope's overhead arc fit in frame. She makes several small, steady two-foot hops, turning the rope with compact wrist movements, elbows close to her sides. The bottle remains visible beside the bench at the edge of frame. Her ponytail bobs behind her.  
No dialogue — rhythmic rope taps, soft landings and light breathing.

3. *(5–7s, tighter insert from the same propped recording)*  
A simple crop onto her lower legs, white socks and the floor. The rope skims the rubber just ahead of her toes, passes beneath both feet during each small hop, then continues behind her. Her ankles and knees absorb each landing. A little natural motion blur follows the moving rope.  
No dialogue. Keep the same jumping rhythm across the cut.

4. *(7–9s, back to the full-body framing)*  
The rope catches lightly against her toes on the next pass. Its rotation stops; she settles onto both feet and takes one small recovery step, still holding a handle in each hand. She looks down at the slack rope, then back toward the lens with an amused, mildly offended expression.  
MILA, with a breathy little laugh: “Okay. Rude.”

5. *(9–11.5s, propped camera, medium crop near the bench)*  
Jump cut: she is crouched beside the bench. She places both handles and the slack rope on the floor, then picks up the same water bottle with her left hand and flips its drinking spout open with her right. Her shoulders rise and fall with slightly quicker breathing; she smiles to herself.  
No dialogue. A small plastic click and quiet gym ambience.

6. *(11.5–15s, closer crop, camera still propped)*  
Still crouching near the lens, she raises the open bottle, takes one brief, ordinary sip, lowers it and swallows. The water tilts naturally inside the bottle. She lets out a small satisfied breath, looks straight into the camera and gives a cheeky half-smile.  
MILA: “Still counts.”  
Finish on her amused expression, with the bottle lowered in her hand.

**Audio and continuity**

Natural American-accented speech with accurate lip sync. Soft gym room tone, rope swishes and floor taps synchronized with each rotation, light breathing, the bottle's lid click and a quiet sip. Leave space between actions and dialogue. No music, voiceover, captions or added comedy effects.

Keep MILA's face, proportions, outfit, hairstyle, lighting and surroundings consistent. The rope remains one continuous cord attached to the same two handles: one rotation per hop, no extra loops, disappearing sections or passage through her body. Both hands hold their respective handles throughout the jumping. The same bottle stays beside the bench until she visibly picks it up.

full_text_zh:
Seedance 2.5 与 Wan 3.0 具有相同的提示

我在@makeugc 上制作了这两个视频。在与 Kling 4.0 进行比较之后，我想看看 Wan 3.0 如何处理相同的跳绳视频博客。

1. 正如我在上一篇文章中提到的，我第一次尝试就得到了 Seedance 剪辑。我给了万三次尝试，选择了第二次，因为那个女人看起来最真实。

2.整体而言，Seedance 剪辑对我来说看起来更真实。万的版本更亮，颜色更丰富，我很喜欢健身房的灯光。这个女人看起来也很可信，尽管我认为万的汗水有点过头了。

3. 每一代的WAN成本要低得多。当您想多次尝试相同的提示时，这一点很重要。

4. 我和Wan一起在其他测试中也取得了不错的成绩。就我个人而言，我还是更喜欢 Seedance 的视频质量。

5. 两种型号总体上都很好地遵循了提示。对我来说最大的区别是错过了跳跃。在万的剪辑中，她在绳子接触到她的脚之前就停止了跳跃，所以这次绊倒感觉像是上演的。我认为她也很早就开始说她的台词了。

对于这样棘手的场景，我仍然会选择 Seedance，但我对 Wan 的表现很满意。您更喜欢哪个版本？

提示⬇️

**相机：**
DV 16mm 磁带摄像机的手持感觉。自拍的健身视频博客：MILA 拿着相机拍摄开场自拍照，然后将其牢固地支撑在矮凳上拍摄跳绳镜头。轻微的手抖、取景未对准、自动对焦延迟以及自拍照中额头被短暂修剪。一旦被支撑，相机就会保持静止；更紧密的插入是同一录音的简单裁剪。随意的硬剪省去了准备时间。摄像机永远不会出现在屏幕或镜子中。

* *: * *
柔软的，稍微模糊的磁带质量，微弱的磁带噪音，在健身房灯光下绽放的高光，微妙的自动曝光波动，柔和的对比度，逼真的肤色。MILA看起来就像一个真实的女人，记录在一个普通的健身房：自然的皮肤纹理，小瑕疵，精细松散的头发和自然的面部表情，在柔和的胶带柔软下仍然清晰可见。柔和的顶灯在她的下巴和脚下创造了可信的阴影。没有美丽的过滤器平滑或有光泽的商业分级。

**风格：**
俏皮、自嘲的健身视频博客语气——最初的自信、几次真正出色的跳跃、一个小错误和一次非常值得的破水。真正的努力与幽默相结合。简短、随意的剪辑、正常速度的动作以及轻松、有趣的结尾。

**特点**

MILA——一位美丽的美国 Instagram 风格的黑发模特和表演者，20 岁。深棕色长发扎成高马尾辫，皮肤焕发着淡淡的汗水光泽，嘴唇有光泽，眼睛富有表情，妆容柔和迷人，戴着精致闪亮的耳钉。苗条的运动身材，胸围非常大，丰满，臀部非常丰满，腰部细，腹部平坦，手臂和腿都很瘦。

她穿着钴蓝色支撑性运动胸罩，细肩带和深汤匙领口露出乳沟，搭配配套的超短合身运动短裤。裸露肩膀、手臂和腹部。白色及踝袜，运动鞋脱掉。她说话带有美国口音。

她的马尾辫随着每次跳跃而自然地略有延迟。她的肩膀保持放松，膝盖在落地时变软，合身的运动服随着身体自然移动。

**环境**

晚上的健身垫区，有平坦的橡胶运动地板、一侧的镜墙和背景中可见的其他设备。柔和的头顶照明。长凳旁边放着一个透明的、半满的水瓶，上面有一个白色的翻盖饮水嘴，位于绳索路径之外。一根普通的深色跳绳，有两个黑色手柄。她上方和周围有足够的净空间，可以容纳完整的绳索弧线。

**故事板（15秒，6个镜头）**

1. *（0–2秒，手持一臂远的自拍）*
米拉带着过于自信的微笑看着镜头，空着的那只手握住两个绳柄。一缕松散的头发靠在她的脸颊上。当她开始将相机向长凳降低时，取景略有下降。
米拉：“这看起来很简单。”

2. *（2–5秒，支撑相机，全身拍摄）*
硬剪辑：摄像机现在放在长凳上，MILA 已经跳到了几步之外。她的整个身体、两个把手和绳子的头顶弧线都适合框架。她进行了几次小而稳定的两英尺跳跃，用紧凑的手腕动作转动绳子，肘部靠近身体两侧。瓶子在框架边缘的长凳旁边仍然可见。她的马尾辫在身后摆动。
没有对话——有节奏的敲打绳索、轻柔的着陆和轻微的呼吸。

3. *（5–7 秒，从同一支撑录音中更紧密地插入）*
她的小腿、白袜子和地板上都有一个简单的裁剪。绳子在她脚趾前面掠过橡胶，在每次小跳时从双脚下方穿过，然后继续在她身后。她的脚踝和膝盖吸收了每一次落地。随着绳索的移动，会产生一点自然的运动模糊。
没有对话。在剪切过程中保持相同的跳跃节奏。

4. *（7-9秒，回到全身取景）*
在下一次经过时，绳子轻轻地抓住了她的脚趾。它的旋转停止；她双脚站稳，迈出一小步恢复，双手仍各握着一个把手。她低头看着松弛的绳子，然后又看向镜头，脸上带着一种有趣、略带生气的表情。
米拉带着喘息般的小笑：“好吧。粗鲁。”

5. *（9–11.5 秒，支撑相机，长凳附近的中等裁剪）*
跳切：她蹲在长凳旁边。她将两个把手和松弛的绳子放在地板上，然后用左手拿起同一个水瓶，并用右手打开其饮水嘴。她的肩膀随着呼吸的加快而起伏。她对自己微笑。
没有对话。小小的塑料咔嗒声和安静的健身房氛围。

6. *（11.5–15 秒，近距离裁剪，相机仍然支撑）*
她仍然蹲在镜头附近，举起打开的瓶子，简单地喝了一小口，然后放下并吞下。水在瓶内自然倾斜。她满意地呼出一口气，直视镜头，露出一个厚脸皮的微笑。
米拉：“仍然很重要。”
完成她有趣的表情，把瓶子放在她手里。

**音频和连续性**

自然的美国口音，口型准确。柔和的健身房音调、每次旋转同步的绳索嗖嗖声和地板水龙头、轻微的呼吸、瓶盖的咔哒声和安静的啜饮声。在行动和对话之间留出空间。没有音乐、画外音、字幕或添加的喜剧效果。

保持 MILA 的脸型、比例、服装、发型、灯光和周围环境一致。绳子仍然是一根连续的绳索，连接在相同的两个手柄上：每一跳旋转一圈，没有额外的环，消失的部分或穿过她身体的通道。在整个跳跃过程中双手握住各自的手柄。同一个瓶子一直放在长凳旁边，直到她明显拿起它。

Seedance 2.5 vs Wan 3.0 with the same prompt

I made both videos on @makeugc. After my Kling 4.0 comparison, I wanted to see how Wan 3.0 would handle the same jump rope vlog.

1. As I mentioned in my last post, I got the Seedance clip on the first try. I gave Wan three tries and picked the second take because the woman looked the most realistic in that one.

2. The Seedance clip looks more realistic to me overall. Wan’s version is brighter, the colors are richer, and I really like the lighting in the gym. The woman looks believable too, though I think Wan went a little overboard with the sweat.

3. Wan costs a lot less per generation. That matters when you want to try the same prompt a few times.

4. I’ve had good results with Wan in other tests too. Personally, I still prefer Seedance for video quality.
